sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared button look
sections.what: Brings in the icons, the class-joining helper and the button styles so page links look like buttons.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond reusing the button look.
sections.watch_out: Depends on the button file; renaming its exports breaks this file.

sections.name: Pagination
sections.title: Wrapper, list and list item
sections.what: Creates the outer navigation area, the row that holds page items, and the slot for each item. Together they lay the page controls out in a line.
sections.why: Likely reason: navigation role and label give standard markup that assistive tools understand.
sections.watch_out: The label text is in English, so non-English apps must change it.

sections.name: PaginationLinkProps (part 1)
sections.title: Page link, previous and next buttons
sections.what: Creates one clickable page link, highlighted when it is the current page, and the Previous and Next buttons built on it with arrows.
sections.why: Likely reason: the current page is marked with aria-current so assistive tools can announce it.
sections.watch_out: Previous and Next do not know the total number of pages; they only follow the target the parent provides.

sections.name: PaginationLinkProps (part 2)
sections.title: Skipped-page marker and export list
sections.what: Shows a three-dot marker for skipped pages and lists the pieces for other files to import.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps long page lists short and readable.
sections.watch_out: The marker is hidden from screen readers, so skipped pages are not announced unless the parent adds text.

summary: Provides building blocks for page controls: previous and next buttons, numbered page links, and a marker for skipped pages.
purpose: Lets a results list show page buttons so the user can move between pages.
why: Likely reason: it wraps standard page navigation markup and button styles so pagination looks like the rest of the app.
how: A wrapper marks the area as navigation. A list and list items hold the page links. Each link is styled as a button and is highlighted when it is the current page. Previous and Next are built on the same link piece. An ellipsis shows skipped pages.
inputs: Page targets and labels passed as props, plus an active flag and size option on each link.
outputs: Rendered navigation markup with button-style links.
risks: This file does not calculate which pages exist. The parent must work out page numbers and supply real addresses or click handlers, since the links are plain anchor tags.
debug: If a link does nothing, check the address or click handler the parent passes. If the current page is not highlighted, check that the active flag is set.
